notes: Elasticsearch 9, 3-node cluster (all master-eligible + data), security disabled. One index per collection with 1 primary shard + 2 replicas, so every node holds every shard (the RF=3 equivalent of the other clustered stacks). Every field indexed at mapping time (inverted index for keyword/text, BKD tree for numeric/geo, HNSW for dense_vector). Eventually consistent for search (30 s refresh; the harness refreshes after load). No multi-document transactions, no server-side joins across indices, no per-document TTL. Any node coordinates writes; the master is re-elected by the remaining quorum when a node dies.

secondary_index.title: Create a secondary index on a non-key field and use it
secondary_index.detail: every field is indexed by default (inverted index / BKD tree / doc_values)

compound_index.title: Compound / composite index over two fields
compound_index.detail: bool query combines per-field indexes; no explicit composite index needed

unique_constraint.title: Unique constraint on a non-key field (duplicate rejected)
unique_constraint.detail: no unique constraint; _id uniqueness only (op_type=create rejects a duplicate _id)

ttl_expiry.title: Native per-document/key expiry
ttl_expiry.detail: per-document _ttl removed in 5.0; use an expiry timestamp + ILM rollover/delete or delete-by-query

text_index.title: Full-text index with tokenised search
text_index.detail: analyzed text fields with BM25 (the core feature)

partial_update.title: Update a single field without rewriting the document
partial_update.detail: _update with a partial doc or painless script (reindexes the document internally)

multi_doc_transaction.title: Multi-document / multi-key ACID transaction with rollback
multi_doc_transaction.detail: single-document atomicity only; no multi-document transactions

tunable_consistency.title: Per-request consistency / write concern / read preference
tunable_consistency.detail: wait_for_active_shards per write; refresh=true|wait_for|false for read-your-write visibility

nested_query.title: Filter on a field inside a nested object

array_operators.title: Query and update array-valued fields (contains, push)
array_operators.detail: arrays are first-class (a field is multi-valued); term query matches any element -> 1044 match 'eco'

server_side_join.title: Join / lookup between two collections inside the engine
server_side_join.detail: no server-side joins across indices (denormalise, parent/join field within one index, or terms-lookup)

graph_traversal.title: Variable-depth traversal over references
graph_traversal.detail: no graph traversal (client-side, or X-Pack Graph explore API)

schema_validation.title: Server-enforced document schema / constraints
schema_validation.detail: explicit mappings + dynamic:strict rejects unknown fields; field data types enforced at index time

change_streams.title: Change feed / watch / keyspace notifications
change_streams.detail: no change feed; poll with a sorted timestamp/_seq_no or use Logstash/change-detection

server_side_scripting.title: Stored procedures / Lua / JS / UDF executed by the server
server_side_scripting.detail: Painless scripts (ingest pipelines, script queries, script fields, _update) -> 2

pubsub.title: Publish/subscribe messaging built into the engine

explain_plan.title: Query plan / profile output for a query
explain_plan.detail: _validate/query?explain and Search Profile API (per-shard query/collector timings, took=17ms)

bulk_import.title: Native bulk import path (bulk API, batch, COPY-like tool)

large_document.title: Store and read back a 15 MB document / value
large_document.detail: 5 MB _source stored (http.max_content_length 100 MB; large text hurts search)

many_fields.title: Document with 5000 top-level fields
many_fields.detail: index.mapping.total_fields.limit default 1000; 5000 distinct fields triggers mapping explosion (use flattened type)

read_from_replica.title: Client can direct reads to a replica / secondary
read_from_replica.detail: reads are served by any shard copy (primary or replica) automatically; ?preference= pins routing

snapshot_backup.title: Online snapshot / backup command available
snapshot_backup.detail: snapshot API into an fs repository under path.repo (S3/GCS/Azure via repository plugins); SLM schedules + retention (exercised in the backup phase)

incremental_backup.title: Incremental / differential backup (file- or segment-level)
incremental_backup.detail: repository stores each Lucene segment once: every snapshot after the first only uploads new segments

pitr.title: Point-in-time recovery from a continuous change log
pitr.detail: no translog replay between snapshots — the RPO is the SLM schedule

slow_query_log.title: Server-side slow-query log with a configurable threshold
slow_query_log.detail: per-index search/indexing slowlog thresholds (index.search.slowlog.threshold.query.warn ...), dynamic, JSON lines with took_millis + source

audit_log.title: Audit / full-query log of statements or auth events
audit_log.detail: xpack.security.audit.enabled needs security enabled (off in this lab); JSON audit of auth/access events

structured_logs.title: JSON-structured server log out of the box
structured_logs.detail: ECS JSON on stdout in the docker image (server, deprecation, slowlog datasets)

runtime_log_level.title: Change log verbosity at run time (no restart)

get_by_key.title: Point read: customer by primary key

multi_get.title: Batch point read: 100 customers by key in one request

update_field.title: Partial update: set one field of a customer

upsert.title: Upsert inventory row by composite key

atomic_increment.title: Server-side atomic increment of a numeric field

batch_insert_1000.title: Bulk write: 1000 events in one request

range_by_secondary.title: Secondary lookup: orders of one customer

range_by_time.title: Range scan: events of one type in a 3-day window

filter_nested.title: Filter on a nested field + top-level field

top_n_sorted.title: Top-N with sort: 10 most expensive active products of a category

join_lookup.title: Orders of a customer with the customer's name (server-side join if the engine has one)

graph_traversal.title: Category ancestor chain of a product (variable-depth traversal)

geo_near.title: Geo radius query on customer locations

transaction_transfer.title: Multi-document atomic transfer between two inventory rows
transaction_transfer.error: Unsupported: no multi-document transactions (single-document atomicity only)

opt01_secondary_index.title: Range scan on events(event_type, occurred_at): no index vs secondary index (both column orders)
opt01_secondary_index.what: an access path that is not indexed is a full scan; composite order matters on B-tree-like engines

variants.name: indexed_field (all fields indexed by default)
variants.error: all fields are indexed at mapping time; opt01 (add a missing index) does not apply

opt02_projection.title: Point read of an order: whole document (with embedded items) vs 3-field projection
opt02_projection.what: returning fewer fields saves serialisation and transfer; some engines still read the whole document

opt03_pagination.title: Deep pagination: offset/skip vs keyset (cursor) at depth 10k and 100k
opt03_pagination.what: offset still walks and discards rows; a keyset cursor seeks directly into the sorted index

opt04_batching.title: Write batching: 2000 events one-by-one vs 2 bulk requests of 1000
opt04_batching.what: round trips dominate small writes; every engine has a bulk path (insert_many, pipeline, batch, _bulk)

opt05_multi_get.title: 100 point reads: sequential round trips vs one multi-get request
opt05_multi_get.what: batched reads (MGET / $in / IN / mget / pipelining) amortise the network round trip

opt06_embedding_vs_reference.title: Order with its items: embedded array (one document) vs referenced (order + items lookup)
opt06_embedding_vs_reference.what: embedding what is read together avoids a second query / join; referencing keeps documents small and items independently addressable

opt07_write_durability.title: Single-document write at each durability / write-concern level the engine offers
opt07_write_durability.what: acknowledgement level (replica acks, fsync, refresh) is the biggest lever on write latency

opt08_read_consistency.title: Point read at each read consistency level / read preference the engine offers
opt08_read_consistency.what: linearizable / quorum reads cost extra round trips; replica reads trade freshness for offload

opt09_connection_reuse.title: Point read with a new connection per operation vs one persistent client
opt09_connection_reuse.what: handshakes (TCP, TLS, auth, topology discovery) dwarf a point read; always pool

write_contention.interpretation: version drifted from applied count: lost or duplicated updates

strategy.tool: snapshot API into a registered repository (type fs under path.repo; S3/GCS/Azure repositories in production) — segment-level incremental
strategy.consistency: per-index point-in-time at snapshot start (immutable Lucene segments; the translog is not included)
strategy.restore: online: delete (or close) the indices, POST _snapshot/<repo>/<snap>/_restore (rename_pattern to restore beside the live index); the fs repository must be the same shared path on every node
strategy.incremental: built in — a repository stores each segment once, the 2nd snapshot uploads only new segments (snapshot.stats.incremental)
strategy.pitr: no; the SLM schedule is the RPO (searchable snapshots / CCR for other goals)
strategy.schedule: SLM policy (cron schedule + retention) executed by the cluster itself — created by the backup phase

backup.slm: SLM policy nslab-nightly: daily 01:30, keep 3-30 snapshots / 7 days

restore.method: DELETE the 8 lab_* indices (by name) + POST _snapshot/nslab/<tag>/_restore

incremental.method: second snapshot into the same repository (only new segments are copied)

strategy.server_log: ECS JSON on stdout (docker image log4j2): event.dataset elasticsearch.server / deprecation / index_search_slowlog / index_indexing_slowlog
strategy.slow_query: per-index slowlog thresholds (index.search.slowlog.threshold.{query,fetch}.{warn,info,debug,trace}, index.indexing.slowlog.threshold.index.*), dynamic; lines carry took_millis, source, total_hits
strategy.audit: xpack.security.audit.enabled (JSON audit of authentication/authorization/run_as) — needs security on; off in this lab
